turns.user: Brainstorm AI product ideas for knowledge workers. Avoid the default AI chat assistant, AI summary tool, and AI meeting-notes assistant. Force distinct causal mechanisms.
turns.assistant:
Here are AI product ideas where the value comes from a distinct causal mechanism—not “ask a bot,” “summarize text,” or “take meeting notes.”

| Product | User | Causal mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision Replay** | Executives, product leaders | Records decisions, assumptions, and outcomes; periodically compares forecasts with reality to calibrate judgment. |
| **Organizational Compiler** | Operations teams | Converts policies into executable workflows, detects contradictory rules, and flags ambiguous ownership before work stalls. |
| **Exception Radar** | Finance, legal, procurement | Learns the normal shape of transactions and surfaces only unusual combinations requiring human review. |
| **Counterfactual Planner** | Strategy teams | Simulates “what would have to be true?” scenarios and identifies the few assumptions that determine the recommendation. |
| **Work Graph** | Large organizations | Reconstructs how work actually moves across people and systems, revealing bottlenecks, shadow processes, and single points of failure. |
| **Expertise Expiry Monitor** | Engineering, medicine, compliance | Tracks which internal knowledge is becoming obsolete as laws, APIs, products, or scientific findings change. |
| **Commitment Ledger** | Cross-functional teams | Detects promises made across email, tickets, docs, and calendars, then checks whether they are being fulfilled. |
| **Process A/B Lab** | Operations managers | Runs controlled experiments on internal workflows and measures whether a process change improves speed, quality, or error rates. |
| **Pre-Mortem Engine** | Project teams | Generates risk hypotheses from project structure and historical failure patterns, then assigns measurable leading indicators. |
| **Knowledge Market** | Enterprises | Routes questions and unresolved issues to employees based on demonstrated expertise and availability—not job title. |
| **Attention Allocator** | Managers, analysts | Estimates the economic value of unresolved tasks and reallocates limited human attention toward the highest-leverage work. |
| **Artifact Linter** | Developers, analysts, consultants | Checks documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and code for cross-artifact inconsistencies before they reach customers. |
| **Institutional Memory Simulator** | New hires, consultants | Lets users test proposed actions against historical precedent, stakeholder preferences, and past organizational reactions. |
| **Negotiation Boundary Detector** | Sales, procurement, recruiting | Learns an organization’s actual concession patterns and warns when a deal crosses an implicit limit. |
| **Research Provenance Engine** | Analysts, journalists, scientists | Maintains claim-to-source-to-transformation lineage so every conclusion can be audited and updated when evidence changes. |
| **Workflow Autopsy** | Customer support, back office | Studies completed cases to identify where humans compensated for broken systems, then quantifies the cost of those workarounds. |
| **Skill Decay Forecast** | Knowledge workers | Predicts which skills an employee is losing through disuse and recommends real work that exercises them before decay becomes costly. |
| **Internal Reliability Score** | Teams and departments | Measures whether requests, handoffs, and commitments are predictably completed, creating operational reliability metrics beyond “busy.” |
| **Assumption Registry** | Product and strategy organizations | Extracts hidden assumptions from plans, assigns owners, and automatically tests them against new evidence. |
| **Change Impact Map** | Enterprises | Predicts which people, systems, policies, and customers will be affected by a proposed change before rollout. |

The strongest wedges, in my view:

1. **Artifact Linter** — immediate value, easy to demonstrate, and naturally embedded in existing workflows.
2. **Commitment Ledger** — painful problem with measurable outcomes and a clear path beyond chat.
3. **Decision Replay** — creates a proprietary dataset around prediction quality and organizational learning.
4. **Change Impact Map** — high-value enterprise problem where better causal modeling directly reduces rollout failures.
5. **Workflow Autopsy** — turns invisible human workaround labor into a quantified automation roadmap.

A useful test for avoiding generic AI products:

> If the product still works when the user never opens a chat window, it probably has a real mechanism.
